purpose: Preserve the async QA / speculative downstream pattern without turning QA into a serial bottleneck or a new acceptance authority.

ideas.name: ASYNC_QA_NOT_SERIAL_GATE
ideas.summary: QA must not unnecessarily delay human access to a useful candidate. Cheap deterministic checks run first; expensive browser/visual/E2E verification may continue asynchronously with explicit QA_PENDING state.

ideas.name: CANDIDATE_CURRENT_PROMOTION_SEPARATION
ideas.summary: Keep existing CURRENT/acceptance authority intact while allowing a new candidate/preview to be visible immediately. Candidate is not silently promoted merely because it rendered once.

ideas.name: QA_STATUS_IN_PRIMARY_CHAT_WIDGET
ideas.summary: Primary Chat should surface concise version/QA state when relevant: QA_PENDING, QA_PASS, QA_REPAIR_IN_PROGRESS, QA_BLOCKED, READY_TO_PROMOTE; do not drown every interaction in QA detail.

ideas.name: INDEPENDENT_VERIFIER_BLOCK
ideas.summary: A universal VERIFY/QA block can be assigned to any disposable /wc shell. It receives artifact/version refs plus executable acceptance vectors and produces evidence, not prose confidence.

ideas.name: QA_DEPTH_BY_RISK
ideas.summary: Do not run image-heavy/browser-heavy QA for every trivial change. Select the cheapest sufficient verification depth from source/static, deterministic harness, integration, served-byte parity, browser interaction, visual/screenshot and full E2E/adversarial regression.

ideas.name: ACCEPTANCE_VECTORS_PRECOMPILED
ideas.summary: Planner/producer should define executable acceptance vectors before implementation when possible: click/action -> observable result, persisted state, served asset identity, privacy/boundary constraints and non-regressions.

ideas.name: SPECULATIVE_DOWNSTREAM_PREPARATION
ideas.summary: While a producer works, spare workers can prebuild tests, fixtures, verifier packets, recovery packets, repair branches and successor work so downstream stages do not wait for the producer to finish before preparation begins.

ideas.name: QA_REPAIR_FEEDBACK_LOOP
ideas.summary: A verifier finding should materialize a bounded repair successor through existing Guide/Integrator/CURRENT. Spare workers may prepare/fix candidate v+1 while the human continues using/inspecting the last safe/current or preview version.

ideas.name: READY_TO_PROMOTE_NOTIFICATION
ideas.summary: When a candidate passes required QA, Primary Chat may show a compact READY_TO_PROMOTE notification/action. If existing policy requires human acceptance, show an Update/Promote action; if existing authority permits automatic promotion, do not invent a new human gate.

ideas.name: VERSIONED_SERVING_AND_BYTE_PARITY
ideas.summary: QA must verify not just source bytes but served bytes/assets and cache/version behavior. Stable subresource URLs can leave users on old code even when gh-pages contains new bytes; publication should use versioned/cache-busted asset refs or equivalent owner-backed serving semantics.

ideas.name: REAL_INTERACTION_QA
ideas.summary: For UI changes, verification should include actual representative interaction where capability exists: page load, target visibility, click/tap, resulting state, persistence and screenshot/visual checks only when materially useful.

ideas.name: QA_AS_RESERVE_WORK
ideas.summary: Surplus workers can consume grounded QA/regression work against recent candidates, pending served verification and historical unverified changes, provided every result has a downstream consumer and fresh human/product work keeps priority.

ideas.name: VERIFY_REPAIR_PROMOTE_PIPELINE
ideas.summary: Reusable flow: PRODUCER -> cheap self-check -> candidate available -> independent VERIFY lanes -> JUDGE disposition -> PASS/REPAIR/BOUNDARY -> repair successor if needed -> reverify -> READY_TO_PROMOTE/current authority.

current_empirical_example.served_asset: gh-pages now contains the new progress-v1.js bytes
current_empirical_example.remaining_failure: served index still references ./progress-v1.js using a stable unversioned URL, so a browser may keep an older cached subresource even after deployment
current_empirical_example.lesson: source PASS and gh-pages byte presence are insufficient for UI QA; served interaction plus asset-version/cache semantics are part of acceptance.

invariants: QA evidence never becomes scheduling or acceptance authority by itself.
Do not hide a usable candidate solely because expensive QA is still running unless risk/policy requires gating.
Do not auto-promote where existing human acceptance policy requires explicit approval.
Do not create a parallel version registry if an existing owner can carry candidate/current refs.
Do not spend visual/browser intelligence when deterministic verification is sufficient.
Every QA failure must either create a grounded repair successor, record a real boundary, or close as non-actionable evidence.
